findings.reason: a node cannot tell whether its target is the descriptionless-recompose recovery (where retiring names breaks a working path) or another recycle path, so it will either disable prose rewriting or decline the section.
findings.text: §11 names "the step that returns a name's source to the pool" as a single step whose defect is leaving names live, but the only step whose log line reads "source(s) returned to 'extracted'" is `reconcile_descriptionless_composed_names` (`imas_codex/standard_names/graph_store/graph_audits.py:2203-2349`), which returns the source deliberately and re-opens the name to `name_stage = 'pending'` so compose rewrites the missing prose — retiring the name instead contradicts the step's own documented reason the source must be freed; at least two other paths emit the same message family (`reconcile_vocab_gaps` at line 1201, `retry_vocab_gap_sources_on_grammar_change` at line 1561), so "the step" does not identify which code the endpoint constrains

findings.reason: the control must be narrowed to the accidental-recycle path, otherwise the node either breaks the descriptionless-name recovery to make its control fail or lands a control it can never turn green.
findings.text: §11 requires a test that "fails when the step is allowed to take the source of a name that is not exhausted", which is exactly what `reconcile_descriptionless_composed_names` does today: it moves a pending (not exhausted) name to `name_stage = 'pending'`, frees its source, and logs that for stranded names the composed source "is the last one they can have"; the section's alternative branch for a non-exhausted affected name ("has its source bound back") restores a binding that step removed because the strict writer cannot re-mint the spelling

findings.reason: the node's design choice (change the default, delete the opt-in, or refuse) is unstated, so three different landings would each claim §12 done and only one matches the author's intent.
findings.text: §12 states that a scoped run executing the pipeline's whole maintenance is the defect, but `sn run` already ships `--skip-global-maintenance` (`imas_codex/cli/sn.py:1764-1780`), documented as bypassing "all global startup, background, and post-drain maintenance writes" for a run bounded by `--focus`/`--batch`/`--name`/`--scope-run-id` and stated "Invalid without an explicit scope"; the out-of-scope write is therefore the documented default with an opt-in escape, and the section never says whether the endpoint makes that opt-in the default, documents the flag as the answer, or removes the option, while its done-when adds the alternative "or refuses to start and says why"
